utterances.text: Look to the end of the message. Was this message sent by the municipal Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: I would now like to ask you to move on to page 9 and to look at 1805, please.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1905, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, then 1905. I'm not sure whether it's 1805 or 1905. It says: "For the Crisis Staff of Dubrovnik from the VPS Boka." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: It says: "We cannot grant your request for introducing a ship line from Sipan to Dubrovnik and back and for starting work on the water pump in Komolac proposed for the 6th of December 1991, nor can we guarantee the safety of the ship and people. We express our readiness to have these issues agreed upon soon, which will primarily depend on the results of the negotiations in Cavtat in December 1991." Signed, VPS Boka. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me now, why does VPS Boka not allow the pump in Komolac to be prepared? Why does it not allow this maritime traffic from Dubrovnik to Sipan? And you said that that was agreed upon on the 5th of December and that there was no disagreement between you.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: You have to ask them about it, not me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Don't you find that strange?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are local negotiations. So you see, I don't even know about this. I'm not even aware of these details. You see, they say that it would be resolved tomorrow, on the 6th of December. This is around 7.00. Well, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: At 1905 on the 5th of December, it says that these requests regarding the repair of the water pump in Komolac and this boat traffic will primarily hinge on the negotiations on the 6th of December, and they were not conducted by anyone else but Admiral Jokic. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I don't find any of this to be strange. I don't see what you find strange.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: It is strange if you say that on the 5th of December, apart from the examination of vessels in the port of Gruz, you agreed everything else with Admiral Jokic, and I put all of this in detail. This would make it seem that the admiral or the VPS Boka does not allow what you agreed upon on the 5th of December.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, whether the admiral informed all the units down there that quickly is something I don't know. I don't know about all the things that happened down there. We could not even establish a cease-fire at 11.00 because, as I was told, not everybody could be notified by then. So I don't find any of this to be strange.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: All right. I would now like to ask you, while you still have the log in front of you, to look at page 7. The time is 1445 hours. It is sent to the Boka VPS.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: What did you say? 14 what?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, I see. So --

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: It is addressed to Boka VPS. It says: "We protest yet again against small arms fire that was directed against the Lapad area from the Laski Brijeg area at 1450 hours on December 5th 1991." Can you explain this to me, because you said that the Port Authority was under you, as minister for maritime affairs. What does this mean when it says "time 1440 hours" and in the message it says that 1450 would be the future time, so to speak?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. But see, you talk about these details. Do you really think that Admiral Jokic informed all the lower level units in Komolac and about the repair of this electricity there?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rudolf, we've dealt with that part of the question when we looked at all these other things. But this is a new thing I would like to deal with.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: What are you asking me about? "We protest yet again against small-arms fire from the Laski Brijeg area directed against the Lapad area at 1450 hours."

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: I'm only interested in the following. This is 1440 --

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: And then it says 1450.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Yes. Referring to the future, as it were. Gunfire that occurs at 1450 on the 5th of December.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with you that it doesn't tally.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Please look at page 15 now. Problems of the same nature, as far as I'm concerned. It is the last item on that page, 1128 hours. 1128 hours.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: This is already the 6th of December. And this is a message for VPO Boka for Admiral Jokic.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Please look at page 16.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: You say --

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That we cannot get into the street, and then they inform me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Yes. And now please look at page 17. It is still the same message. Please look at the middle of the sentence that says "Now it is 1210, and occasional gunfire is still coming from Zarkovica." Have you found that? It's on page 17.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And the signature bears the name of Davorin Rudolf. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you explain this to me: The message is at 1128, and reference is made to 1210. It's as if you were saying it's 1210 now and there is gunfire coming from Zarkovica.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot explain. But this is authentic. I actually wrote this.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: You mean it's your handwriting?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm referring to the time -- the content, actually. The content is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: You have no explanation for these differences in time?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: I would now like to ask you to look at page 7. Again, we've come to the message at 1445. It is still the 5th of December 1991.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: In that message, does it say that the Crisis Staff of the Municipality of Dubrovnik claims that there was no cause given by our side for this incident, as far as this individual gunfire is concerned?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did the JNA lodge a protest when the Crisis Staff claims that there was no cause given from their side?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I haven't seen this. This is probably the first time I'm reading this. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: On the 5th of December, were you informed of some protest lodged by the JNA?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking me a lot. I don't know. I really cannot answer with any certainty. The Yugoslav People's Army did not protest, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Please look at page 11 now. And the time is 0855. Or rather, 0955, I'm sorry. It is the last time marked on that page.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: So this is a message for you.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: From the Boka VPS.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And it says "We are making enormous efforts to stop the clashes caused by shooting from Srdj and Lapad. We ask you to intervene immediately to stop this clash at 1115 hours today." And then a meeting is proposed.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: The signature, VPS Boka. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Since this is the 6th of December, is the VPS Boka lodging a protest with you there, stating that the clash occurred because gunfire was opened from Srdj and Lapad, and they seek your intervention in order to stop the fire coming from there?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what is written here. This is at 9.55. The cease-fire agreement was supposed to come into force at 11.15. In the meantime, there was fighting. In the fighting, of course, the people of Dubrovnik fought as best they could. The cease-fire was not in force yet. But I can tell you that all the messages that I received from the Military Naval Sector of Boka, I checked all of them immediately. I would telephone and ask, "What's going on?" "Is that the way things are?" "Please be careful."

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: All right. Please look at page 12 now.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: The time 10.20. You signed this. It says: "We accept a strict cease-fire as of 11.15."

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: "For practical reasons, we cannot come to the meeting by 1200, so we propose that the meeting be held at 1330 hours or as soon as possible." So that's your answer in response to the previous message. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Are you giving any comments here regarding allegations of fire from Lapad and Srdj?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you, through the municipal staff or Lieutenant Colonel Nojko Marinovic, take any steps following the proposal of the Boka Naval Sector to prevent or stop further fire from Srdj or Lapad?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: The cease-fire hadn't entered into force. Look at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: It was 10.55, and it was supposed to enter into force --

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Do you mean to say that it was allowed to go on firing until that time?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to both sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at page 12 again. Time 10.20.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: 10.27, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just one correction. On page 50, line 21, my question was "10.55" in the transcript, and I said 10.20, as written in the radio log. If that correction could be made, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rudolf, so the time is 10.27 on page 12 of this radio log.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: It's a message addressed to you by Admiral Jokic who is asking Mr. Davorin Rudolf, minister, to come as soon as possible because "I am late for pressing previous engagements of official nature." Did you receive this message?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Just allow me to finish. At 10.27, it says here, the message is addressed to you, if I'm not mistaken, until that time, until 10.27, that is, by that time you had telephoned Admiral Jokic twice already.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. To correct the record, please, if it is being read from the log, on page 12 in the English, at he bottom it says: "For D. Rudolf - Admiral Jokic asks Mr. D. Rudolf to come to the meeting as soon as possible because later the admiral has pressing official engagements." It does not mention "previous."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rudolf, so by 10.27 when you received this urgent message from the admiral, you had already had those two telephone conversations with him you testified to.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: In those telephone conversations, did the admiral tell you anything about his official obligations or engagements?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: This time, 10.27, did you know at that time what was that pressing official engagement he had?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Look, please, at page 13. This is your answer to Admiral Jokic, your reply to his earlier message.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean at 10.45.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's my reply.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: You say the cease-fire is accepted, has been accepted as of 11.15.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that, right there below.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Now, look, please, at page 14, time 11.05.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: This is another message addressed to the Boka Naval Sector, and it is signed on page 15 by the municipal Crisis Staff of Dubrovnik. Right?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Look at the bottom of page 14 now. There's a sentence that reads: "The Defence Forces of the Republic of Croatia responded only after the infantry and tanks came within 200 metres of Srdj." 200 metres of Srdj. Did you, since you were in touch both with the Crisis Staff and with the Lieutenant Colonel Nojko Marinovic, have any information to that effect that morning?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had received information that battles had begun up there on Srdj Hill, and at one point, Nojko Marinovic told me that the troops had even entered the Srdj fortress.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: After that sentence on page 14, it goes on to say: "We deny carrying out any acts of provocation or activities from Srdj and Lapad that would have been cause for the cease-fire violations." The municipal Crisis Staff seems to be denying these actions emanating from Srdj and Lapad. And when we were reading the message from 10.27, you said that it was allowed to go on firing from Srdj and Lapad before 11.15.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, Dubrovnik was defending itself as best it could, as best it was able, until the beginning of cease-fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: I understand that. I'm just asking you -- or rather, I'm going to ask you if you see any discrepancy between this message of the Crisis Staff and the previous message of 10.57, because in this one the Crisis Staff is denying.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: What are you driving at? What do you find odd about this?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, 10.57, I don't see a reference to a 10.57. And if in fact it is 10.20 --

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: It is 10.27.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: The record says 10.57, and just to make clear what is said, which I think the transcript picked up as "cease-fire was accepted at 11.15," then "... has been accepted as at 11.15," what it in fact says on page 12 for the 10.27 -- sorry, page 13, which is actually 10.45, it says "The proposal for a cease-fire as of 11.15 hours has been accepted," just to make sure the record is straight as to what is said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Let us move on, Mr. Rudolf. Look at page 15, please, of this radio log. The time is 11.28. It's at the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: It's a message addressed to Admiral Jokic by you.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that for the first time in this message reference is made to the shelling of the Old Town? It's on page 16.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: It says: "The Old Town was shelled. Fires can be observed in several places." The time was 11.28. By that time, you had two telephone conversations, and you had already exchanged similar messages by radio. Is this the first time that you are mentioning to Admiral Jokic the Old Town, at 11.28?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I mentioned Dubrovnik, I meant the parts of Dubrovnik inside and outside the Old Town. I wrote here about the bombing of the old part of the town because we were able to see it from Hotel Argentina. We were able to have a partial view. We couldn't see what was going on behind us, where there were some explosions, so when I made reference to Dubrovnik, I meant both the Old Town and the other parts.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: I understand that. What I want to know is that by 11.28, or before 11.28, did you put a special emphasis on the Old Town? Did you make special reference to it?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't think it was necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me, if you can remember, between 8.00 and 9.00, 9.30, on the 6th of December 1991, did you have those two telephone conversations with Admiral Jokic and his ADC?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: When you first got him on the phone and spoke to his ADC, he told you that he did not believe there was shelling.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not that he didn't believe it; he said: "We are not attacking Dubrovnik."

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: All right. So then you turned away the receiver for him to hear the sounds.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did he then hang up or what?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he said he was going to get the general on the phone when he heard the sounds.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: So after a while, you re-established the connection?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And then you spoke directly to Admiral Jokic?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us exactly what you told him.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told him the same thing. I told him we had agreed on a cease-fire yesterday, and you are firing again. And I turned away the receiver again. He was a bit breathless and -- in fact, you're asking me what I told him. I told him that they were shelling Dubrovnik despite our agreement of the day before. And to that, he replied, if I remember well, that it was not being done on their orders, that it was preposterous, that it was mad. And he apologised. You have to understand the situation as it was. All I cared about was to have that cease-fire in place. He told me that we should come to Cavtat, and we were unable to get into the street in the first place. What mattered most was goodwill that was necessary for that cease-fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Again, about that 6th of December, did you spend all that day in Hotel Argentina?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Were the ECMM monitors with you all the time?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you see Mr. Hvalkof there?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, you described the view you had from Hotel Argentina of the Old Town. In the course of the 6th of December, did you hear or see any action of the Croatian forces from the territory of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: The entire city. It was fighting, you see. We were in the hotel all that time. The hotel faced the sea. All we could see was the sea and the shells flying. They were shelling the Old Town, the ramparts, and we could hear the gunfire. Some shells were falling on the hotel and on the annex building we were in. It was logical to assume that there was some fire opened from the Croatian side as well, but how and where from exactly, we couldn't see from our position.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: In all that racket, the noise of shelling, gunfire, you could not distinguish between fire, the sounds of fire from one side and the other?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did the local -- did the local media and the local population of Dubrovnik with whom you were in contact say that the JNA was opening fire on Dubrovnik from its ships as well?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: On the 6th of December?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 21 of your statement, you say: "Despite widespread reports of the local media and claims of the population, I did not see JNA vessels firing on the Old Town. I did not see any JNA boats."

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That came later. In the media when I read the reports, people had very different views often it. People saw it very differently. Some said that fire was opened from the sea as well. But I did not see anything of the kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I can just have a minute. Exhibit P61, tab 32. I would like to show that document to the witness. Again, from Witness Hvalkof.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: No microphone for the counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Here we see a message that should be forwarded to the naval sector Boka command, a radiogram. "We strongly protest against the absolutely unprovoked strong artillery fire this morning at 0550 hours from the sector of Strincjera and Dubrava on the Srdj feature, and tank mortar and ship artillery fire on Dubrovnik." Signed by the Dubrovnik Crisis Staff, dated 6th December 1991, with indications of all the addressees.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my opinion, this is not correct, especially this last part, the types of fire originating from vessels, if they mean from the sea.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Yes. In this protest of the Crisis Staff, they specify artillery fire opened from ships.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I know, there was no such fire opened from the sea.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Do you know everything?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is there anyone who knows everything? First of all, I would have seen it because we were facing the sea at the time. Second, I'm absolutely -- I'm sure that I would have been informed. You see, there are all sorts of interpretations and reports. I read some of them concerning the role of Admiral Jokic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Do you see to whom this document was sent?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: The European Mission.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Counsel and witness are speaking at the same time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] ECMM, including Davorin Rudolf.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you receive this notification?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, do you know what hell is? Dubrovnik was hell. Fire was all around us. We couldn't see what was falling where. I personally did not see ships attacking Dubrovnik. Whether anyone else felt it or assumed it, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: I'm interested to know, did this message reach you? Because it was addressed to you.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the hell that reigned there, it went unnoticed by me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me, on that day, the 6th of December 1991, did you have any contacts with the members of the Dubrovnik Crisis Staff by phone or did you see them personally?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not with the members. But I was in touch with Poljanic and with some representatives. I don't know which members of the Crisis Staff were there. And of course, with the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Give us some names, please.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spoke most frequently with Poljanic. Did I mention Mladenic? When I say I was in touch, you should understand that all the three ministers in my group were in touch with those people. Everything we did, we did together.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: So on the 6th of December, you contacted people from the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were in the Old Town, we were in the Hotel Argentina. We were unable to go out, to leave the hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: I understand all this.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: So all that was said was said on the phone.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: I have to remind you again, because we are being reminded again, to make pauses between questions and answers because we're speaking fast.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I won't be needing this document again. And now, with the usher's assistance, P61, tab 30, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rudolf, you have before you a Prosecution exhibit. This is a log sheet related to the 6th of December. And this is a type of diary that was kept by Mr. Per Hvalkof from the European Community. Could you please look at the time of 0600 hours.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Could you read it.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Shelling from land and sea towards the fortress close to the TV tower Srdj and the harbour commenced."

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: At this particular point in time in the log sheet, does Mr. Hvalkof say that shelling commenced from land and sea?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what he says. I was telling you about my impressions. If you want to check this out exactly, you have the man behind you. Ask him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately, he was not there either, so I cannot ask him either.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they certainly know whether they targeted Dubrovnik from land and sea.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: What I want to ask you is --

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really did not see any ships and nobody told me about any ships.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: I understand because of the situation, because of everything that you told us about the 6th of December, how you felt and the position and the Hotel Argentina where you were, and also your confirmation that you could not see everything that was going on on that particular day. Isn't that right? And I also put the protest letter of the Crisis Staff to you, and now I've shown you Mr. Hvalkof's log sheet. Do you allow for this possibility, that perhaps you did not see it but that ships were actually in action?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see that. Look, were you ever at the Argentina Hotel? Well, since you know, it's on the eastern side of Dubrovnik. This is practically where the town of Dubrovnik starts. And we saw the sea right in front of us, so if a ship had passed by, it would have to pass by the hotel, in front of the hotel. We would have to see it. I'm just telling you about what I know, what I saw, and I cannot assert anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me, now, let's explain this: Could you see from the hotel the harbour of Gruz?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Could you see the top of the sea from Babin Kuk onwards?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, as for the harbour of Gruz, the JNA ships could not have reached them without passing in front of the Argentina Hotel. Well, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Is there anything else you wanted to say? Did you wake up around 7.00?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Is it possible that this happened before you woke up?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Objection, speculative. I think the question was asked and answered a number of times as to what he really saw or believed to have seen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Carry on, Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Let us proceed, Mr. Rudolf. I would like to ask you to look at this log sheet again. The time of 0920 hours.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: It says here: "Minister Rudolf spoke to Admiral Jokic's secretary. Promised meeting scheduled for 11.00 at Cavtat." Does this note reflect the messages, more or less, the ones hat we read out earlier on from the logbook of the Port Authority?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I did not talk to a secretary, a female secretary. It was a man. But this is wrong. This is a misinterpretation. It's not 11.00. The meeting's not 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, well, you know, I don't know everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at the next page and the time of 11.10.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: "Minister Rudolf speaks to Zagreb. The message from the naval base in Boka Kotorska, JNA will cease-fire at 1115 hours. A meeting in Cavtat is planned for 1330 hours." Does this note reflect the situation that we saw from the Port Authority logbook?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: It reflects the facts, and also it says here "God willing."

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Please look at 1203: "Machine-gun fire near the hotel from the Croatian side - artillery active again, sporadic." So by the hotel that you were staying at, did you hear any gunfire opened at close range?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Which hotel does he mean anyway?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: The Argentina Hotel.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: On the 6th of December, did you see Mr. Hvalkof at the Argentina Hotel? Did you contact him?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. You know, there were quite a few people there. Everybody was downstairs. Everybody who was at the hotel. And now, who all the people were...

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Please, look at 1410 hours. That's on the next page. "Minister Rudolf informed me that he wrote a proposal of the agreement."

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot find that. 1410?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Yes. 1330 until 1400, and then it says 1430 --

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. I got the pages wrong. What did you say? 1410? What does it say? Possibly. Possibly. Now, to tell you the truth, I cannot remember now whether it was that particular conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Please look at 1430. "Minister Rudolf receives message from Admiral Jokic who apologises for the shelling and informs that it is out of JNA control."

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But look, 1430, that's not the time when I got the message from the admiral. It's probably when I told him. You see, these men in white were there, as we call them, the representative of the United Nations, et cetera. Now, whether I talked to him personally or not, I really don't know. But here he says that I did, so I probably told him this. As you can see, he encouraged me in terms of the negotiations. Have you read this sentence?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I read it?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Please look at the time of 1610 on the last page.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: It says: "Only a few shells since 1600 hours. Minister Rudolf tells me that General Strugar has ordered immediate cease-fire. However, sporadic shells still fall." By 1610, as recorded here, did you have any contact with General Strugar?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think these times are correct. I really would have to check. I received a radiogram from General Strugar only at 4.30, or perhaps this should be checked. So you see, these times are not correct. But I did receive a radiogram from General Strugar who said that he ordered a cease-fire. I think that the Prosecution showed me this radiogram.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: We'll get to that document, too. Please look at 1914. It says: "See note at 1610. Translation and copy of General Strugar's message sent to the regional centre of Split." Could that be the radiogram of General Strugar?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the first and only one I got from General Strugar. After that, I answered him in the evening, but then you know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We no longer need this document. I would like to ask for P61, tab 27 and tab 36.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: As for the document that is before you, it is also a Prosecution exhibit which was tendered during the testimony of Witness Hvalkof. I would just like to ask you to look at the last sentence in the second paragraph. "The Croatian government issued strict instructions to the authorities in Dubrovnik not to hand over their weapons." Does that accurately reflect the position of the Croatian government?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we please look at the next document, now. Do you have it in front of you?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: The radiogram.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Please, then. Does it say here "Radiogram from the Boka VPS for the Dubrovnik Crisis Staff"?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: For Mr. Davorin Rudolf, minister.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me, we saw from the previous questions during this discussion of ours, we used the radio log of the Port Authority. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: This radiogram connection was established between the Port Authority and the Military Naval Sector of Boka?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Since I'm a layman, you explained this coastal radio --

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: -- of Dubrovnik, or rather the Port Authority. Do you know, how does it function and with who? Is it a pure radio communication or what?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was the only possible communication at that time because there was nothing else. This is radio communication with ships, and to tell you the truth, I really don't know where this was, the radiogram. Or rather, I don't know where he was, in what town and how this link was established.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Another question I have for you, being a layman myself, when it says "radiogram," is that communication by way of speaking? Is it two speakers who converse, or is there any written trace of this?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course, you can speak. But this is in writing. So it can be done in writing and verbally. To put it in lay terms, it is both a fax and a telephone, so to speak.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: To when it says "radiogram," that is --

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does not relate to speech, because then it would be radio-communication, you see. This is written, gram, you see, radiogram.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And what kind of equipment is used for this kind of correspondence by way of radiogram?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: They have special equipment for receiving and transmitting these radiograms. Well, look, I'm not a technical person but it's a type of fax. Nowadays, there are all sorts of wondrous things that exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: During the course of the 6th of December, did you receive any other radiogram in which General Strugar was mentioned to you?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Please look at --

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the answer is no.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Please look at the time. You see before you these different markings. They are probably fax markings underneath the text. It says "monitors, Dubrovnik, 6th December, 1714."

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And further up, above the radiogram, you have "1914" as the time. And then there is a telephone number, 38 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please slow down. The interpreters do not have the text or the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: So would 58 be right for Split?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says remote here "3858" -- what was it that you said?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Would that be the number -- or rather, is the area code for Split, or was the area code for Split at the time 058?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is 021 now. I don't know what it was then. It is possible that it was 058. You know, it's hard for me to say now how they did it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Obviously, this document was sent on two faxes at least.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know really. I really don't know. I did not even check this. It was the text that really mattered to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: All right. Could you please keep this document in front of you. And now I would like to ask you to look at the radio log again. And let's compare something.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let's.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: The radio log, page 22, please. Please look at page 22 and look at the time, the last number that is entered. Is it 1440, this time here, 1440?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, round that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: So it's around 1400 hours, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, somebody changed this. I guess it's like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Oh, somebody changed it.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Message for the Crisis Staff of Dubrovnik, and it says: "Our forces ceased firing on all parts of Dubrovnik at 1115 hours." As far back as 1115 hours. "We absolutely reject the possibility of our troops firing at the said time, especially on the Old Town. Boka VPS Command."

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Please look at that and compare it to the radiogram, the one that you have before you. It also continues at 1550 in the radio log. So the message is identical in the radio log and in this document that is before you. "JNA forces this morning were attacked from Srdj and Babin Kuk without any cause. Our forces responded by gunfire, but on my orders the units stopped fire at 11.15. But your forces did not respect this cease-fire. And therefore it can be concluded that the buildings in the old part of Dubrovnik are being damaged by fire coming from your forces." Except for this last part, the last part of the sentence when it says what is damaging buildings in the old nucleus of Dubrovnik, at the beginning of the message, is it similar to that which is mentioned at 1440 from the Boka VPS? Because the time of cease-fire is referred to and how it happened, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that the only thing that is said and that is the same is the cease-fire of 11.15. But this text here at 14-whatever, there is no reference to attacks being made without cause.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Rodic, I'm afraid we're going to run out of time on the tape. So I've let you go on because you seem to be following a clear lead, but we'll have to have the second break now and then we'll carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. May I ask that the witness be shown Exhibit P61, tab 33.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Are you tired, Mr. Rudolf?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You see, there's no more coffee.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: We'll try to bring to this an end today, if we can. You have in front of you a Prosecution exhibit, which is a letter dated 6th December that you addressed to General Strugar. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: That letter has to do with the radiogram we reviewed a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: If you would kindly look at paragraph three from the top, you say that you arrived to Dubrovnik and Cavtat with two members of the government of the Republic of Croatia because you received guarantees from the Supreme Command of the armed forces of the SFRY and the command of the VPO, the naval district of Split, for a safe and unhindered trip to the negotiations with representatives of the Yugoslav Army in Cavtat.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 2, you say "I'm writing all this, General, because of your radiogram because you said that the Croatian forces set fire to Dubrovnik." Did this radiogram irritate you so much that you had to write the letter to General Strugar, since the radiogram was signed by him, or rather, his name was on the radiogram?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: You invited the general to come to Dubrovnik, and: "To be informed by" -- and you say, rather, "the Minister of Defence, General Kadijevic, ordered an investigation into the damage or destruction inflicted on Dubrovnik today. I am convinced that this investigation will be conducted in a proper manner." On that day, the 6th of December, did you have any contact with General Kadijevic?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: How, then, did you know that General Kadijevic ordered an investigation?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the message of Admiral Jokic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And you expressed here your conviction that the investigation will be fair and that you will undoubtedly be informed of its results.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I invited General Kadijevic to come to Dubrovnik and I offered guarantees on behalf of the Croatian government for his safety. And I said that since the general didn't come, his officers should come to Dubrovnik and see for themselves the destruction.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: On the 8th of December, when those two officers with the cameraman came to Dubrovnik, were you there?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: The first reference to General Kadijevic is in the context of this investigation. In fact, the first reference, as far as you are concerned, is made by Admiral Jokic in that message sent to you.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Admiral Jokic mentioned him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: In view of your telephone conversations with Admiral Jokic, one that you had with him personally and another with his ADC, the numerous radiograms that were exchanged on that day between Dubrovnik and the naval sector, is it the case that General Strugar was mentioned to you for the first time in relation to this radiogram that we reviewed?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the first time. Sorry, on the 5th, when we started our negotiations.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: I'm speaking about the 6th.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was the first time, on the 6th.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown Exhibit P61, tab 38.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rudolf, is this the agreement that you signed together with two other ministers, your colleagues, on behalf of the Croatian government on one hand and Admiral Jokic signed it on behalf of the armed forces of the SFRY?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: It was signed on the 7th December 1991?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Point 1 speaks of the cessation of armed clashes, armed hostilities, in the entire area of Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Point 2 says that "In order to ensure this permanent cease-fire, both sides will strive to a reduction of troops and weapons."

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Was that in keeping with your negotiations of the 5th of December?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure that we discussed this particular detail on the 5th.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Look at item 3.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: It says: "On the 7th of December at --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: -- "the JNA is in agreement to allow transport, passenger and other traffic, with previous announcement and control of cargo in Gruz harbour." "Starting as of December 7 1991 at 1800 hours JNA agrees that ships sail in and out of the Gruz harbour for traffic and passengers."

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At 1800 hours, the cease-fire entered into force for the entire area, for this entire territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Does this agreement, Mr. Rudolf, apart from this inspection in the Gruz harbour make reference to anything regarding the blockade of Dubrovnik, as we discussed in the beginning?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, that is a matter of interpretation, whether the blockade was lifted or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Does this agreement make any reference to an undertaking that JNA naval ships would not be used in that part of the sea?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. Maybe we should read the text, but I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: So this control of ships in Gruz harbour is the only outstanding matter from the 5th of December which stood in the way of the signing of this agreement?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Look at one more thing in Article 1 of this agreement, the penultimate paragraph of this article: "Each side shall, within the limits of its competencies, institute proceedings against offenders of these terms and inform the other side thereof."

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you really reach an agreement that both sides will investigate any offences and inform the other side?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me, during your stay in Dubrovnik, during those ten days or so, because you stayed on after the 7th of December for a couple of days --

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Starting from the 7th of December 1991 until you left Dubrovnik, were there any minor incidents?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not as far as I can remember. Not in the city of Dubrovnik. Certainly not.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me, after the 7th of December, did you have occasion to speak to Admiral Jokic?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: On the 7th of December before you signed this agreement, you explained already how this meeting between you and Admiral Jokic ran, at that meeting did he mention to you that he would carry out an investigation?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: It has been 12 years since that day. I really couldn't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can I remind you in paragraph 32 of your statement reference is made to the meeting of the 7th of December when you say: "When I finished, Jokic unexpectedly and obviously very sincerely stood up and apologised for the incident. He promised that he would carry out an investigation, and he repeated Kadijevic's apology."

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is true, that last part. In the context of all our discussions, that can be understood --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. I would like to just correct the record. Paragraph 32 reads: "When I finished, Jokic in an unexpected and visibly sincere manner stood up and apologised for the incident. He promised an investigation..." It doesn't say that he would carry out an investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am reading from the B/C/S version of the statement. The witness is here to tell us what exactly Admiral Jokic said on the 7th.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You see, he said that in the context of our discussion. It's difficult to say after so much time. But from the entire context of his apology, when he said that General Kadijevic would send an apology to me and even the European Community, it's difficult to say anything for sure now.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: All right. But did you receive this on the part of Kadijevic, from Kadijevic?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I personally didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may ask for tab 39 of P61 to be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Before you review this document, Mr. Rudolf, regarding precisely this meeting of the 7th of December, did Admiral Jokic at one point react vehemently while you dictated the text of the agreement?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said "The army's supposed to restore electricity, the water supply. It's all about the army. What are you supposed to do?" And the three of us looked at each other, and we said "We accept the agreement. What else can we promise?" It was just a reaction. I already told you about it. And he reacted once more when we were writing in Croatian.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Is this reaction reflected in this excerpt from your book?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which one?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: The excerpt from your book "The War We Didn't Want," when you describe how he stood up at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe I described all that, and all the radiograms. It's all in the book.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you have a look at this document?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am looking at it right now. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, on the 6th, on the 7th, on the 12th, or maybe on one of the later days, did you have any contact regarding these events in Dubrovnik of the 6th of December with Admiral Brovet, with General Kadijevic?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did Admiral Jokic maybe send you this document? Did he tell you anything about the contents of this document?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm seeing it for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Do you know that this commission representing the naval sector of Boka and consisting of two officers and one cameraman came to Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Were you there on the 9th?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe so. On the 9th.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did anyone from the Crisis Staff or the command of the defence of Dubrovnik inform you on the 8th when this talk with the JNA commission was over as to the results and what was agreed?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if they told me what was agreed but I believe they were accompanied by a deputy by the name of Simonovic. He was an officer. I believe he was a deputy of Nojko Marinovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: What about Mico Mihocevic? Was he the Croatian liaison officer with the ECMM?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether he was an officer at the time. But he was liaising with these representatives of the European Community. He brought telegrams, things like that. But I don't think he was an officer at that time. Or maybe he was. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: I'm going to remind you. In your statement, paragraph 22, you say: "Later on that morning, I got a telegram that Mico Mihocevic, a Croatian military liaison officer with the ECMM, gave me, saying that Jokic had sent a message that due to operational reasons, the cease-fire should come into effect at 11.15."

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's a colonel now, I think. If I'm not mistaken. Maybe he was an officer. I'm not sure. But he was liaison.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Even before your testimony, you corrected this statement.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: You corrected the name of Mico Mihocevic.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I'm not sure about this. But that's easy to establish. That's easy to find out.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: At any rate, on the Croatian side, he carried out those duties?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me one more thing in relation to the 5th of December. You finished the meeting at Cavtat, and you said to us that after that you provided information in Dubrovnik about the results of these talks. Can you tell us who it was that you talked to? Who did you convey this to?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everybody. If you wish, everybody that I was in touch with. Of course, to Commander Marinovic, then the president of the city, Di Mistura. I believe the Europeans too, so everybody. Because this was good news. How can I put it?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believed that at that time, we had reached an agreement. There was a blockade, but I was sure that on the following day at 10.00, we would sign the agreement that we had actually concluded. To tell you the truth, we would have signed this even if the blockade had stayed on because it was so important to have a cessation of hostilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I really need to pause a bit longer. In view of the terms of the agreement, the final agreement that we saw, Admiral Jokic, had he insisted, on the 10th of December, that ships be examined or checked at sea, would you have signed that agreement, too?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I, speaking for myself, yes, I would have.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Once again, I would like to ask for tab 35 from P61 to be shown to the witness again.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: You have this before you, don't you, this letter of Admiral Jokic dated the 6th of December.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is this famous - what can I say - telegram, message, whatever you wish to call it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: I'm going to read a sentence out to you, and I'll ask you for clarification. It says here General Kadijevic sent a message to you and to the Monitoring Mission of the European Community in Dubrovnik concerning "an energetic investigation about our responsibility and the perpetrators of this incident." Since you said that you did not contact General Kadijevic on the 6th of December --

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: -- how do you understand this, then? That General Jokic was transmitting this kind of message from General Kadijevic to you?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is informing me about this message.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, the next sentence says: "At the same time, we expect to have responsibility established on your side as well, and in order to have a full clarification of all circumstances with regard to the events of last night and this morning." So "this morning" is the 6th of December, and "last night" is the 5th of December, isn't it? What is your understanding of this?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: My understanding of this is that it is his message. And of course I informed Mr. Nojko Marinovic about this, but I informed the command about all these events and all these things. But the answer I got was that this was written in a merely perfunctory manner, and all the answers I got were quite identical, that from the Croatian side, this attack on the 6th of December in the morning had not been provoked.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me, after this letter, you saw Admiral Jokic on the 7th of December. Was there any mention by Admiral Jokic of this expectation that an investigation be carried out on your side, too?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot give an answer with any certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: You cannot remember whether he asked you something about that?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And when he gave you the letter, you said that he gave you General Strugar's letter in a blue envelope with an apology regarding the event of the 6th of December.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: On that occasion, was Jokic mentioned in relation to the investigation, or Kadijevic, Strugar? Can you remember any of this at all?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: He just handed over the envelope. He just said "This is an envelope for you from General Strugar." Nothing else. He never mentioned Strugar again. Of course, he did mention Kadijevic saying that an apology was underway.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: All right. And please look at item 4 regarding these proposals of his; that is to say, that ships be checked in the port of Gruz. When you received this message with this kind of proposal, bearing in mind the proposal made in item 4, did you believe that a final agreement would be reached?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: That was the only controversial matter?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I repeat, this telegram was of exceptional importance to us. I've already said that I read it out to the citizens of Dubrovnik. And perhaps I can tell you about a particular detail. Thanks to this message that I read, and this agreement, I was declared an honourary citizen of the district of Dubrovnik. So I only did what I thought was best. This was no special merit of mine. But this shows how important this was to the people from Dubrovnik. So I, as a man from Split - this is also noteworthy - was declared an honourary citizen. I don't really want to go into any other interpretations, but the people of Dubrovnik really thought this was so important, and I am an honourary citizen of Dubrovnik. Probably the first person from Split ever to hold that position in Dubrovnik in view of the rivalries between the two cities. Perhaps the other people present here are not aware of the magnitude of all of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Later on, when you reported about your meeting with Admiral Jokic, did you have any special talks with any of the members of the Crisis Staff of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of them. All of them. You see, everybody came and said "What happened?" "What did you achieve?" And I was convinced that we had reached an agreement except for this one particular item. And I thought that in this entire story it wasn't all that important, that one item.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me, on the 5th of December, especially in relation to this particular matter, did you talk to Commander Nojko Marinovic?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I certainly did. I must have.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: In view of the results of the talks, did you give him a particular task in relation to the implementation of the agreement?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You see, my understanding was that we had reached an agreement on cessation of hostilities. And I transmitted this to Nojko Marinovic, and I think that he took this to be a type of order.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, in connection with this, on the military side in Dubrovnik, were any special instructions issued to the Crisis Staff or to the military units in Dubrovnik? In terms of having absolute observance of the cease-fire agreement, was there anything in writing or verbally? Were there any orders whatsoever? Did anybody report to you about that?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: You say that you don't know that.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't. I don't. I didn't check it, you see. I thought that we had reached agreement and that the following day we would be signing this agreement on the following day at 10.00. There must have been a bit of euphoria, too. And let me tell you one more thing: Before that, I had signed two agreements that were actually observed in Zitnic. The agreement was not signed on the first day, only on the second day. And it was observed. And also the one up there that was signed in Rijeka, and the one in Zitnic, and the one in Dubrovnik. All three were actually observed, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me one more thing, the letter you mentioned that you received in a blue envelope on the 7th of December, do you remember the content of the letter perhaps?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was a letter in which General Strugar said that a unit of the JNA got out of control and that it started an attack on its own bat, and he expressed his regrets because of that attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Rudolf, thank you for your answers. I have completed the cross-examination, Your Honours. Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Rodic, thank you very much for that and to your precise attention. Ms. Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Mr. Rudolf, after the attacks on the Old Town of Dubrovnik on the 6th of December, were you, or to your knowledge any other official of the Croatian government at any level, ever informed of whether or not an investigation by the JNA did take place as to culpability; and if so, who the culpable parties, if any, were found to be?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally do not know any details. But I have to tell you that the Yugoslav People's Army was a well-organised army. I was sure that they had started an investigation and that they knew exactly what was going on. I even told you this. Eight or nine years later, I was prepared to meet with General Jokic -- with Admiral Jokic and to ask him what happened on this other side. I knew what happened on the Croatian side. But I assumed that the Yugoslav People's Army, after all these assurances, must have carried out an investigation. But I don't know the results.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: So you are not aware of any matter of record that came from the JNA about either the fact of an investigation having been carried out or the results. Is that what you're confirming? You simply did not hear about it?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Would you expect to have heard about it, given your very central role in bringing about the negotiations finally on the 7th of December 1991? Would you expect -- you looked at me surprised. Perhaps my question was not clear to you.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Given your role, would you have expected to have been apprised of any results of any investigation that may have been carried out?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally, no. But the Croatian government, yes. Of course I expected the Croatian government to be informed. You see, I was just a minister in the government.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And you were not informed, or were you informed, by anybody in the Croatian government about the outcome of any possible investigation?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Was it your view that given your assertion that the Croatian side did not provoke any attacks, that there was no need for an investigation by the Croatian side on -- and I'm talking about only the events of the 6th of December.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: You indicated that after December 7th 1991, or at least end of December 1991, or perhaps you can give us the date, when was the last time that you had any contact with Admiral Miodrag Jokic?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the 7th of December, I never had any further contact. I read an interview of his in the Borba daily newspaper, but -- that's a Belgrade daily. But I never saw him, met up with him, talked to him. Never.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I want to clarify: You mentioned something about Vis, a meeting at Vis. Was that subsequent to the 7th of December?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And are you indicating that Admiral Jokic was not involved -- you did not see Admiral Jokic at that particular meeting?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The commander of the entire navy was there, Admiral Mile Kandic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: But not Admiral Jokic?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your indication now that if you had to revisit the agreement, that the bigger concern was ending the hostilities as opposed to necessarily lifting the blockade, are you able to indicate whether or not the hostilities, which I assume -- I'm making the assumption you mean the shelling. Am I correct, the shelling by forces under the JNA control, was the bigger concern?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And you had indicated earlier that the timing of this particular set of negotiations was important or you would not have known what would have happened to Dubrovnik. Could you perhaps explain your comment. What was it about the fate of Dubrovnik that was particularly worrisome for you if hostilities did not cease?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, you warned me that we don't have a lot of time, but allow me to tell you the following: Had we not managed to establish this telephone communication, the town would be destroyed. As far as the shelling is concerned, we did manage to reach the cease-fire, and the fire was abating, and finally, around 5.00, the hostilities stopped. You see, we're sitting here in a room in peace, in a beautiful city, and what I experienced in Dubrovnik was hell. It was real hell. I told you it was a brutal attack against a very fine, peaceful town. And had we not managed to stop the shelling, I don't know what would have remained as far as the town was concerned. It would have been set on fire. That is one thing. Secondly, you see, we in Croatia always wondered why Dubrovnik had been blocked, why it had been besieged from land. And there are different versions. But I'll tell you one. When I negotiated with Admiral Kandic in Vis, the admiral told me that the navy would withdraw from Vis but not the island of Lastovo, and these are two islands that are pretty nearby. The island of Vis is very well fortified. It had a lot of military infrastructure and equipment. And Lastovo is a small island, relatively insignificant. And I wondered why he said that. When I same in Split I looked at a map, and when you draw a line from the confluence of the Neretva River towards Italy, towards the open sea, the island of Vis is to the west of that line and the island of Lastovo is to the south. Since the area up to Ston was occupied, I think - this is my interpretation - this was perhaps one of the possible boundaries that was being considered at the time between Croatia and the other state.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: You were shown a document from - and you don't have to pull it out, I'll present to you, in the interests of time - from Prosecution's Exhibit P61. It was tab 39, which was a commission report by -- sent under the name of Admiral Jokic to Admiral Brovet, summarising the commission, in other words, the persons who had gone to Dubrovnik from the JNA to look around at the damage. I would like to ask you, please, one of the comments at the very end of the report is: "It is the opinion of the commission that there is no substantial damage to the cultural and historical monuments." I think the usher has just placed it in front of you, if it may be of some assistance. It's just above -- on the second page -- are you looking at where I'm reading from, where it says: "It is the opinion of the commission that there is no substantial damage..." "The origin of all the damage cannot be stated with certainty and the perpetrators named because it is obvious that a lot of the damage was not caused by the attacks from outside of the Old Town centre." My question to you is do you agree with the opinion of the commission that there was no substantial damage to the cultural and historical monuments in the Old Town as a result of the shelling of the 6th of December? Do you concur with that?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not agree. And I must say that this is not at the level of the Yugoslav Army. No matter what it was like.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Was there in Dubrovnik among the people a sense, if you were able to get the pulse of the town from your time there, a sense of needing to engage in and some agreement to stop the hostilities and to improve the conditions that the citizens of Dubrovnik were living under? Was there a perceptible feeling from your having been there?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Look, that was our only way out.
